name: Glide Sync Bass
description: After Attack Magazine's low analog bass on an eight-voice polysynth template: played solo with a long glide, VCO-1 at 16', VCO-2's pulse a little detuned and synced, its width moved by the LFO, the low-pass near 4 with a little resonance and ENV-2 on it, the level held. From the article: the glide, the feet, the pulse, the sync, the detune, the LFO on the width, the cutoff, the resonance, ENV-2 on the filter and the level's envelope; estimated: their conversion to the panel and the envelope's amount.

name: Growl Bass
description: VCO-2 swinging VCO-1's pitch at audio rate, deep enough to lift VCO-1 from 32' to 16' where the key plays, heard through a resonant filter: a growling, gritty bass.

name: Octave Dance Bass
description: A saw at 8' over a pulse at 16', a resonant filter plucked short at each note: the bouncing octave bass of 1980s dance music, played as low and high eighths.

name: Pedal Bass
description: After Nick Magnus's analog basses in Sound On Sound, whose bass-pedal sound is saws set some seven cents either side with a sine under them: here two saws at 16' fourteen cents apart through a low, warm filter. From the article: the saws and their spread; estimated: the rest. Its sine is left out: the instrument has two oscillators.

name: Pluck Bass
description: A pulse over a saw an octave under it, a resonant four-pole struck open, the level dying under the key: a short, plucked bass.

name: Round Bass
description: VCO-1's square at 16' and VCO-2's saw an octave under the keys into a resonant filter the envelope snaps open at each note, played solo.

name: Rubber Bass
description: A pulse over a saw an octave under it through the two-pole, high in resonance and snapped by its envelope, gliding from note to note: a round, rubbery bass.

name: Sub Bass
description: VCO-1's triangle at 16' and VCO-2's sine an octave down, the filter low: a deep sub that is felt more than heard.

name: Sync Bass
description: VCO-2 reset by VCO-1 at 16' and thrown up by the envelope at each note: a snarling, vocal bass.

name: Synth-Pop Bass
description: VCO-1's narrow pulse at 8' over a saw an octave under it, a quick bright pluck settling half way: the driving bass of a synth-pop single.

name: Unison Bass
description: After Nick Magnus's analog basses in Sound On Sound, where the eight-voice polysynth's bass is a unison stack of widely detuned voices: every voice on one key, spread wide, through a four-pole the envelope snaps open. The idea is the article's; the values are estimated.

name: Unison Sync Bass
description: Every voice on one key, each VCO-2 reset by its VCO-1 and swept by the envelope: a huge, tearing bass.

name: Upright Bass
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's upright bass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. VCO-1's triangle at 16' with VCO-2's pulse at 8' synced to it and blipped up by ENV-1, a closed four-pole opened a little by ENV-2, both envelopes shorter higher up: a plucked double bass.

name: Carillon
description: After the maker's sound-design article on bells and mallets for a 1985 polysynth of theirs: VCO-2 cross-modulating VCO-1, the filter low with the keys following it well, a long fall. From the article: the low cutoff, the key follow and the fall; estimated: the cross-modulation, the envelope on the filter and the interval, an octave and a fifth less a quarter of a semitone, where the cross-modulation's rise in pitch puts the bell's strongest partials on the key and its octave.

name: Cross Bell
description: VCO-1's triangle with VCO-2's sine an octave and a fifth up swinging its pitch at audio rate: clangorous partials over a soft strike that rings out.

name: Cross Chime
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's chime, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. VCO-1's triangle at 4' cross-modulated by VCO-2's saw an octave up, the four-pole shut at its foot and resonant, opened wholly by ENV-1 and following the keys fully: a bright chime that rings on.

name: Digital Chime
description: After the maker's sound-design article on bells and mallets for a 1985 polysynth of theirs: VCO-1's square at 8' cross-modulated by VCO-2's pulse at 4' three semitones up, the filter near 6.5 struck by a very short ENV-1 at full amount, the level falling over a few seconds. From the article: the waves, feet and interval, the cross-modulation, the cutoff, ENV-1's amount and the envelopes' shapes; estimated: the cross-modulation's depth and the times on this panel.

name: Glass Chime
description: VCO-2 reset by VCO-1 two octaves up, its pitch swept down by a quick envelope, ringing out: a glassy, high chime.

name: Music Box
description: VCO-1's triangle at 4' with VCO-2's sine two octaves over it, struck and dying fast, higher notes faster: a small music box.

name: Steel Pan
description: After the maker's sound-design article on bells and mallets for a 1985 polysynth of theirs: VCO-2 half a semitone off VCO-1, the filter at its foot with a large ENV-1 striking it open, a fall of a second or two. From the article: the detune, the shut filter, the envelope's amount and the fall; estimated: the cross-modulation and its conversion to the panel.

name: Toy Mallet
description: After the maker's sound-design article on bells and mallets for a 1985 polysynth of theirs: the chime with VCO-2 at 2', six semitones and a third up, and a shorter fall. From the article: the interval and the fall; estimated: the cross-modulation and the filter.

name: Tubular Bell
description: After the maker's sound-design article on bells and mallets for a 1985 polysynth of theirs: VCO-2's square nine and a half semitones up, reset by VCO-1 and heard alone, the filter near 7.5 struck by a quick ENV-1 at full amount, the keys following a little, the level falling over a few seconds. From the article: the waves, the interval, the sync, the mix, the cutoff, ENV-1's amount and the envelopes' shapes; estimated: the conversion of the times to this panel.

name: Vibraphone
description: After Paul McGeechan's vibraphone patch for the instrument in Electronics & Music Maker's Patchwork (1984): VCO-1's triangle at 8' and VCO-2's pulse, the cutoff and resonance just over their first marks, the two envelopes' decays a little apart, the LFO let in late on the filter. From the text: the waves, the feet, where the cutoff and resonance stand and the delayed LFO on the filter; estimated: every other value, since its chart could not be read.

name: Xylophone
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's xylophone, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. VCO-1's triangle and VCO-2's pulse at 2' synced to it, both pitches blipped by ENV-1, the two-pole struck open by ENV-1 and following the keys, the level falling fast, the higher keys faster.

name: Brass Stab
description: After Francesco Preve's sound-design article for the maker's software model of the original, on the maker's site: two saws a few cents apart, ENV-2 throwing the filter wide (amount about 7) from 3.4 with a quick attack and full sustain, and a hair of ENV-1 on VCO-1's pitch for a blip at the front. From the article: the saws, the detune, the cutoff, the envelope amount and ENV-2's times; estimated: the conversion of its scale to the panel's, and the blip's direction (here it rises; the article's falls, by an inverted ENV-1). Its echo is left out: the instrument has none.

name: Fanfare Brass
description: The saws behind a filter thrown wide at once and settling bright, the keys opening it further up: hard, brassy blasts for a fanfare.

name: High Brass
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's high brass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two saws at 8', VCO-2 a little sharp, the four-pole half shut with the whole of ENV-1 rising over a third of a second and falling to under half: trumpets over the low brass.

name: Horn Section
description: A pulse and a saw apart by a few cents behind a filter that the first envelope swells open over a quarter of a second and lets settle, the level following a little behind: a section of horns.

name: Low Brass
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's low brass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two saws at 16', VCO-2 a little sharp and a little louder, through the four-pole half shut with the whole of ENV-1 swelling it open: the instrument's own low brass.

name: Random Brass
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's sample-and-hold brass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. The low brass with resonance, its cutoff stepped at random by the LFO's random wave once its delay has passed: brass that bubbles as it holds, from 1980s progressive rock.

name: Soft Horns
description: After Nick Magnus's analog brass in Sound On Sound: the French horn as the brass made slower in attack and decay, with less of the envelope, more sustain and longer releases; here VCO-1's triangle under VCO-2's saw through a closed filter. The idea is the article's; every value is estimated.

name: Swell Brass
description: After Gordon Reid's brass patch for a classic monosynth in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: one saw at 4' behind a filter shut to its foot, a large envelope opening it over some 600 ms and falling over 800 ms to half, the keys following fully, the level rising in 100 ms. From the article: the saw at 4', the shut filter, the envelope's amount, times and sustain, the full key follow and the level's attack; estimated: the conversion of each to this panel and the little resonance.

name: Sync Brass
description: VCO-2 reset by VCO-1, the first envelope throwing its pitch up a little at each chord and falling back, under the brass's filter: brass with a hard, metallic bite.

name: Synth Brass
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's synth brass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two saws at 16', VCO-2 a little sharp, through the two-pole shut low with some resonance and the whole of ENV-1 on it, opening in a few tens of milliseconds and falling back to a fifth, the level falling to some 60 %: the classic polysynth brass.

name: Dance Stab
description: A saw and a pulse an octave up, a bright resonant filter snapped shut in a tenth of a second: the off-beat stab of the 1980s dance floor.

name: Detuned Stab
description: The saws far apart with VCO-2 a fifth up and a little flat, a resonant two-pole and a quick fall: a sour, wide rave stab.

name: Funk Pulse Chord
description: Both pulses narrowed and swept by the first envelope as the filter snaps open: a tight, quacking funk comp.

name: Inverted Funk Chord
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's funk patch, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. A saw at 16' and one at 8' through the four-pole open and at full resonance, the inverted ENV-1 pulling it down at each chord and letting it back, a little LFO on it: a juicy, quacking funk comp.

name: Poly Stab
description: The saws through a resonant four-pole that the envelope flicks open, a short level: chords that punch and get out of the way.

name: Pop Chord
description: A pulse and a saw a few cents apart, a quick bright attack settling to a steady chord: the synth-pop rhythm part.

name: Resonant Chord
description: The two-pole high in resonance, the envelope sweeping it down through each chord: a vocal, wah-like comp.

name: Gong
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's gong, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Every voice on one key, VCO-1's pulse, its width swept by ENV-1, cross-modulated by VCO-2's sine five semitones up, the resonant four-pole pulled down by the inverted ENV-1, the level held and a long release: a struck gong.

name: Laser Zap
description: Both oscillators thrown three octaves up by the first envelope and falling within a moment: a laser zap.

name: Random Spheres
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's last patch, a cosmic effect, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. VCO-1's saw at 16' cross-modulated by VCO-2's pulse at its low range, its pitch stepped widely at random by the LFO, through the open four-pole with ENV-2 on it and a release that never ends: the music of the spheres.

name: Ratchet Drone
description: VCO-2 at its low range, a few hertz the keys do not move, swinging VCO-1's pitch: a held note that rattles and pulses like a machine.

name: Space Drone
description: VCO-1 at 32' and a detuned saw under a closed, resonant filter the LFO drifts open: a dark, slow drone for space.

name: Unison Fifth Drone
description: After the maker's article on six of their classic instruments: a saw and a pulse a fifth apart in unison, the width moved by the LFO at full, the two-pole half open with little resonance and the keys following, ENV-1 sweeping it slowly, the LFO let in late, a slow, sustained level. From the article: the waves, the fifth, the unison, the width's source, the slope, the cutoff, the key follow, the sweep and the LFO's delay; estimated: every value.

name: Wind
description: VCO-2's noise alone through a resonant filter the slow LFO sweeps up and down: wind across an open plain.

name: Init
description: Both oscillators' saws, the second a few cents sharp, through the four-pole low-pass half open with its first envelope on the cutoff: where a sound is begun.

name: Clav Keys
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's electric clavichord, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two narrow pulses at 16' through the four-pole open and following the keys fully, the inverted ENV-1 closing it over each note, the level struck and falling to nothing: a funky comp, like an electric clavichord's.

name: Mellow Tines
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's mellow electric piano, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step; estimated: VCO-2's interval, which the drawing leaves between 4' and 2', and the tremolo's depth, a step of four on the hardware. VCO-1's pulse with VCO-2's sine an octave and a sixth up, through a resonant four-pole at rest, the level struck and falling to a little, a tremolo on it, the higher keys shorter.

name: Poly Keys
description: A pulse and a saw an octave up, the filter struck open and falling, the level decaying under a held key: a bright comping keyboard.

name: Soft Blip Keys
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's mellow blip, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two saws at 8', VCO-2 blipped up by a short ENV-1, through the four-pole shut low with ENV-2 opening it as slowly as the level rises, the keys following fully: soft, round keys with a pitch blip at the front.

name: Square Organ
description: VCO-1's square under VCO-2's sine an octave up, the filter open and still, the level on and off with the key: a simple combo organ.

name: Synth Piano
description: VCO-1's triangle and a saw, struck bright and falling away like a piano string, the keys shortening the higher notes.

name: Tine Keys
description: VCO-1's triangle touched at audio rate by VCO-2's sine two octaves up, a struck bright edge fading to a pure tone: an electric piano's tines.

name: Breathy Unison Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for the lead of a 1984 synth-pop single credited to the original: a saw in unison spread some twelve cents, noise beside it at some 40 %, the low-pass near 7.5 with a little resonance, a slow vibrato of some 28 cents, full sustain and a release near a second. From the recipe: the saw, the unison and its spread, the noise, the cutoff, the resonance, the vibrato and the level's times; estimated: their conversion to the panel.

name: Chip Unison Lead
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a 2010 film score's chiptune lead on an emulation of the instrument: a square in unison, a little spread, the filter wide open. From the breakdown: the square, the unison and the open filter; estimated: the spread and the envelopes.

name: Cross-Mod Lead
description: VCO-2's sine an octave down swinging VCO-1's pitch both ways at audio rate, VCO-1 heard alone through a resonant filter: a gritty, buzzing lead with a growl under it.

name: Fifths Lead
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's fifths patch, for a lead or a bass, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two pulses at 16' a fifth apart, their width swung by the LFO, through the two-pole shut low, high in resonance and opened wholly by ENV-1, the keys following fully. VCO-2's fine is set to play the fifth in tune.

name: Fusion Poly Lead
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's jazz-fusion lead, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Two pulses at 16', their width swept by ENV-1, through the four-pole shut low and opened wholly by ENV-1, falling to a high sustain, played poly so a line can hold its chords; the bender bends the filter more than the pitch, as the sheet says.

name: Fuzz Lead
description: After Gordon Reid's fuzz-guitar patch in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: a narrow pulse beside a saw, the width following the envelope as each note dies down, played solo. From the article: the pulse and the saw, and the width on the envelope; estimated: every value.

name: Glide Saw Lead
description: Two saws played solo with a long portamento between the notes and a filter the envelope pushes open: the classic gliding analog lead.

name: Negative Sync
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's first patch, a sync lead with ENV-1 turned over, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step; estimated: the assign mode, unison as the sheet suggests for a lead. VCO-2's pulse at 4' reset by VCO-1's at 16', a slow LFO let in late swinging it widely, the four-pole open and resonant and pulled down by the inverted ENV-1 at each note: a surging, vocal lead.

name: New Wave Sync
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's sync patch named for a 1979 new-wave single, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Every voice on one key, VCO-2's pulse at 16' alone, reset by VCO-1's square and thrown far up by a long ENV-1, through the two-pole with ENV-2 on it, the level falling slowly under a held key: the bright, sweeping sync riff of new wave.

name: Octave Unison Riff
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a 2010 film score's riff on an emulation of the instrument: every voice in unison, two saws an octave apart with the lower louder, a middling resonance and a decay of some ten seconds. From the breakdown: the unison, the octave and the balance, the resonance and the decay; estimated: the cutoff, the envelope's amount and their conversion to the panel.

name: Pulse Glide Lead
description: After Syntorial's recipe for a famous 1980s film-theme lead credited to the original: a narrow pulse played solo with a touch of portamento, its width moved by the LFO at some 2 Hz, two oscillators four cents apart, the filter open near 8.5, a quick attack and a short release. From the recipe: the pulse, its width moved by the LFO and how much, the detune, the cutoff and the level's times; estimated: their conversion to the panel and the glide. Its echo is left out.

name: Soft Sine Lead
description: VCO-1's triangle and VCO-2's sine, a vibrato that waits before it starts: a soft, flute-like solo voice.

name: Sync Lead
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's sync lead, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. Every voice on one key, two saws at 16', VCO-2 reset by VCO-1 and thrown up by ENV-1 deeply and falling back, the two-pole open with some resonance and following the keys fully: the tearing sync lead.

name: Sync Sweep Lead
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's sync sweep, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step; estimated: VCO-2's interval, which the drawing leaves between five and six semitones. Every voice on one key, VCO-2's pulse reset by VCO-1's saw at 16' and swung widely by a slow LFO let in late and by ENV-1, the LFO moving the width and the resonant four-pole too: a wailing lead that never sits still. The bender sweeps VCO-2 alone, as the sheet says.

name: Unison Lead
description: Every voice on one key, the saws spread apart, a little glide and a resonant filter: a huge, thick lead.

name: Wah Lead
description: The two-pole high in resonance, swept up by the envelope at each note and falling back: a vocal, wah-wah lead.

name: Choir Pad
description: VCO-1's triangle and VCO-2's sine, slightly apart, through the high-pass and a resonant two-pole between them, with a delayed vibrato: soft voices singing 'ooh'.

name: Dark Pad
description: VCO-1's square at 16' under VCO-2's saw, the four-pole nearly shut: a deep, dark bed that sits under everything.

name: Hollow Pad
description: After Francesco Preve's sound-design article for the maker's software model of the original, on the maker's site: VCO-1's square and VCO-2's pulse ten cents apart, the LFO moving the width a little, ENV-1 holding VCO-1 a shade sharp, the filter open near 7.3, a slow attack of ENV-2 and a long release. From the article: the waves, the detune, ENV-1's shape and its small pull on VCO-1, the width's source, the cutoff and ENV-2's times; estimated: their conversion to the panel, the LFO's rate and the filter's envelope, left off.

name: Night Pad
description: The saws behind a closed filter that a slow LFO drifts, the attack and the release both several seconds long: a slow, distant pad for film and ambient music.

name: Pulse Swell Pad
description: After Syntorial's recipe for the keys of a 2016 television theme credited to the original: a thin pulse at 4', two oscillators apart, a resonant band of some 900 Hz that follows the keys fully and a slow LFO on it, swelling in over five seconds and cut off short. From the recipe: the pulse at 4', the band's corner and resonance, the key follow, the LFO on the cutoff and the level's times; estimated: the band made of the high-pass and the low-pass, and their conversion to the panel.

name: PWM Pad
description: Both oscillators' pulses, their width swung by the slow LFO, through a soft filter: a shimmering, moving pad.

name: Rising Pad
description: The filter shut at each chord and opened by an envelope that takes seconds to arrive: a pad that rises out of the dark as it is held.

name: Slow Strings
description: VCO-1's pulse, its width swung by the LFO, under VCO-2's saw a little sharp, slow to swell and slow to let go.

name: Smooth Pad
description: After Francesco Preve's sound-design article for the maker's software model of the original, on the maker's site: both saws, even in the mix and a few cents apart, the filter well open with a little of ENV-2 on it, ENV-2 slow in at about 4 and out at about 5. From the article: the saws, the mix, the detune, the cutoff, the envelope's source and amount and its times; estimated: their conversion to the panel.

name: Sweep Pad
description: The saws through a resonant filter that the slow LFO sweeps up and down: a pad that breathes in and out.

name: Verse Pad
description: After MusicRadar's walkthrough of the synths of a famous 1983 pop album: two detuned saws through a low-pass near 650 Hz, a little LFO on one oscillator for a chorus-like drift. From the article: the saws, the cutoff and the LFO on one oscillator; estimated: the detune, the LFO's rate and depth and the envelopes.

name: Warm Pad
description: Two saws apart by some fifteen cents behind a closed four-pole, slow in and slow out: a warm, wide bed.

name: Synth Cowbell
description: After Gordon Reid's cowbell in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: two square-ish tones some 6.3 semitones apart through a band near 2.6 kHz, with a short fall. From the article: the two tones and their ratio, the band's place and the short envelope; estimated: the band made of the high-pass and the two-pole, and every value on this panel.

name: Timpani
description: After Gordon Reid's timpani in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: tones near a fifth apart, struck with no attack and falling as long when let go as when held, a darker strike under it. From the article: the fifth and the envelope's shape; estimated: the rest. Its other partials and its ring-modulated layer are left out: the instrument has two oscillators.

name: Anthem Pluck
description: After Francesco Preve's sound-design article for the maker's software model of the original, on the maker's site, on the pluck of a famous 1983 rock anthem: two saws a few cents apart through a filter open near 7.3 with a little of ENV-1, both envelopes falling to nothing over half a second or so. From the article: the saws, the detune, the cutoff, ENV-1's amount and both envelopes' times; estimated: their conversion to the panel.

name: Inverted Pluck
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's pluck with ENV-1 turned over, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. VCO-1's pulse at 16' with VCO-2's sine under it, the width moved by ENV-1, the four-pole open and resonant, pulled down by the inverted ENV-1 a quarter of a second into each note and let back as it decays: a plucked wah against a bright, held tone.

name: Jazz Guitar
description: After Gordon Reid's jazz-guitar patch in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: a pulse of some 25 %, the filter and the level on one envelope, no attack, a decay near 6.5 and a sustain near 4. From the article: the pulse and the envelope; estimated: the filter and its conversion to the panel.

name: Koto Pluck
description: A narrow pulse through the two-pole high in resonance, snapped open and ringing down: a koto-like plucked string.

name: Picked Guitar
description: After Gordon Reid's electric-guitar patch in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: a pulse louder than a saw beside it, both envelopes falling to nothing, the filter's sooner than the level's. From the article: the pulse and the saw and their balance, the envelopes' shapes; estimated: every value on this panel.

name: Pizzicato
description: The ensemble's saws plucked short through a soft filter: plucked strings.

name: Pop Pulse Pluck
description: After Syntorial's recipe for the pluck of a 1982 synth-pop single thought to be the original: a pulse, two oscillators three cents apart, a low cutoff the keys follow half way, a quick filter envelope of some 100 ms and a level falling in some 230 ms. From the recipe: the pulse, the detune, the key follow, the envelopes' shapes and times; estimated: the cutoff and the envelope's amount on this panel. Its echo is left out.

name: Resonant Unison Pluck
description: After Reverb Machine's breakdown of a 2010 film score's pluck on an emulation of the instrument: unison, the low-pass near 100 Hz high in resonance with a little envelope, a decay of some four seconds. From the breakdown: the unison, the cutoff, the resonance, the small envelope and the decay; estimated: their conversion to the panel.

name: Synth Pluck
description: Two saws, the filter struck open by the envelope and shut again within a moment: the plain synth pluck.

name: Arpeggio Bass
description: The arpeggiator up an octave in sixteenths through a low chord, each step a short pulse bass: a driving sequenced bassline from held chords.

name: Falling Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator down three octaves in sixteenths, each step a bright saw pluck.

name: Random Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator picking the chord's notes at random over two octaves in sixteenths, each a soft, bell-like ping: a twinkling texture.

name: Rising Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up and down three octaves through the keys held, each note a square and a saw an octave over it, plucked bright.

name: Soft Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up and down two octaves in eighths, each step a soft triangle with a gentle release: a calm, lilting pattern for a ballad.

name: Sweeping Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up two octaves in sixteenths through the two-pole high in resonance, a slow LFO sweeping the cutoff under it: a sequence that opens and closes.

name: Sync Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up two octaves in sixteenths, each step VCO-2 reset by VCO-1 and swept down by the envelope: a zapping, metallic sequence.

name: Synth-Pop Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up two octaves in sixteenths with the song, each step a pulse plucked through a resonant filter: the chiming arpeggio of early 1980s synth-pop.

name: Synthwave Arpeggio
description: After MusicRadar's walkthrough of an arpeggio in the original's style on an emulation of the instrument: the arpeggiator up and down, VCO-1's pulse a little narrow, VCO-2's saw an octave up and quieter, the filter near 300 Hz with a little resonance, ENV-1 short with a little sustain, a hair of slow LFO on VCO-2. From the article: the mode, the waves, the width, the octave, the mix, the cutoff, the envelope's shape and the LFO; estimated: the range, the rate in time with the song and their conversion to the panel.

name: Triplet Arpeggio
description: The arpeggiator up and down two octaves in eighth-note triplets, each step a square plucked bright.

name: Arpeggio and Strings
description: Split at G under middle C: the arpeggiator runs the bass notes up two octaves in sixteenths as plucks, the string ensemble held over them.

name: Bass and Brass
description: One of the factory setups listed on the maker's 1981 patch sheets for the original: the upright bass under the split and the synth brass over it, each read off its sheet (the panel's settings were measured off the sheet's drawing, to about half a step; estimated: the split point, at G under middle C).

name: Bass and Pad
description: Split at G under middle C: the warm pad over it and a round square bass under it.

name: Bass and Strings
description: Split at G under middle C: the strings over it and a plucked bass under it, each patch on four voices.

name: Brass over Strings
description: Dual: both patches on every key, the synth brass's swell over the strings' slow bed.

name: Lead over Bass
description: Split at G under middle C: a bright sync lead over it and a plucked bass under it, for playing a line and its bass at once.

name: Octave Brass Layer
description: After Nick Magnus's analog brass in Sound On Sound, where a big-band section is the brass with a second layer an octave up: dual, the synth brass on the upper patch and the lower an octave over it, a little quicker and quieter. The layering is the article's; the values are estimated.

name: Organ and Bass
description: Split at G under middle C: a square-and-octave organ over it, gated, and a round bass under it.

name: Pluck and Pad
description: Dual: a bright pluck strikes each chord and dies away while a slow pad swells in under it.

name: Strings and Bell
description: Dual: the string ensemble with a gently cross-modulated chime struck on each key, ringing over the bow. Deeper, the cross-modulation would raise the chime a semitone over the strings.

name: Strings and Tines
description: A dual pairing suggested on the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the low strings: the low strings over the mellow electric piano on every key, each read off its sheet (the settings were measured off the drawings, to about half a step; estimated: the balance).

name: Bright Strings
description: After Francesco Preve's sound-design article for the maker's software model of the original, on the maker's site: VCO-1 at 4' and VCO-2's pulse an octave over the keys, six cents sharp, the width set a little by hand, the high-pass near 3 and the low-pass open near 8.4, ENV-2 bowing in slowly and letting go slowly. From the article: the feet, the waves, the detune, the width, both filters and ENV-2's times; estimated: their conversion to the panel. Its chorus is left out: the instrument has none.

name: Chamber Strings
description: After Nick Magnus's string patches in Sound On Sound, where the eight-voice polysynth's strings are two saws with a fast vibrato of some 8 Hz on one: VCO-2 shaken by the LFO through the two-pole with a touch of resonance and a gentle bow. From the article: the two saws and the vibrato's rate and target; estimated: the rest.

name: High Strings
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's high strings, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step. A saw and a pulse at 4', VCO-2 a little sharp, the LFO swinging the width and VCO-1's pitch, through the two-pole well open with some of ENV-2: the violins over the low strings.

name: Low Strings
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's low strings, its best-known string sound, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step; estimated: VCO-1's vibrato, drawn near 1.5 and set at 1 here, where the model's depth law is steeper at its foot. A saw and a pulse at 16', VCO-2 a little sharp, the LFO swinging the width and VCO-1's pitch, through the two-pole open with ENV-1 on it, both envelopes slow and shorter higher up.

name: Mellow Strings
description: Read off the maker's 1981 factory patch sheet for the original's mellow strings, every setting measured off the sheet's drawing to about half a step; estimated: VCO-1's vibrato, drawn near 2 and set at 1.2 here, where the model's depth law is steeper at its foot. A saw and a pulse at 8', the LFO swinging the width and VCO-1's pitch, through the two-pole open and still: a soft section.

name: PWM Strings
description: After Gordon Reid's string-machine patch on a Japanese polysynth in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: both oscillators' pulses swept from square to thin by the LFO, close in pitch, VCO-2 an octave down, the filter half shut with no envelope and some key follow, the level a slow trapezoid. From the article: the pulses and their sweep, the octave, the filter and the trapezoid; estimated: the values. Its random LFO on VCO-1 is left out: the instrument has one LFO, here on the width.

name: Solo Violin
description: After Gordon Reid's bowed-string patch in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: a saw at 4' with the low-pass lowered and the high-pass raised, a slow bow, a vibrato of some 6 Hz that waits before it comes in, and a glide just off its foot, played solo. From the article: the saw at 4', the two filters' directions, the attack, the delayed vibrato and the glide; estimated: the values. Its formants are left out: the instrument has no band filters.

name: String Ensemble
description: After Gordon Reid's string patch on a later eight-voice polysynth in Sound On Sound's Synth Secrets: two saws at 8', VCO-2 four cents flat, a light LFO on VCO-1, the low-pass near 4.7 with a little of ENV-1 and the keys following, ENV-1 at 1.5/0/9.9/3.9 and ENV-2 at 4.5/0/9.9/5.4, and a second copy layered detuned: here the lower patch in dual, eight cents the other way. From the article: the waves, the detune, the filter, both envelopes and the layer; estimated: the LFO's rate and depth on this panel, the layer's detune. Its chorus is left out.
